clue.text: Sailor on oceans reported guiding light

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it, so the first-named piece goes second
something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want what the word sounds like when spoken

parts.note: oceans of something means loads of it; LODES (veins of ore) is pronounced the same
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman out on the oceans is said to have spotted a guiding light.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B, so the sailor comes last. 'Oceans of' and 'loads of' both mean lots.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar is a star used to steer by, especially the Pole Star, and figuratively any guiding principle.

clue.text: Toilet's even vacant and free

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet; with the 's it becomes 'loo is'

indicators.note: a vacant word has had its contents emptied out, leaving just its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word once its middle is emptied

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the toilet is unoccupied and costs nothing to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an intensifier, but it is the word to be emptied; 'vacant' sits naturally beside a toilet, hiding its role.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something, such as a knot or a grip, is to slacken it or undo it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Regretted going north taking to byroad?

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece is wrapped around another
in a down clue, travelling north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: rued means regretted
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver who took a side road and wished they had not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is not a link word here but the letters placed inside the turned-around word.
explanation.definitionFit: A byroad is a minor side road, and a diversion off the main route takes you along such a roundabout way.

clue.text: Remorse of cheat covers sweetheart

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering something means sitting on top of it, so one piece comes first

parts.note: a sham is a fraud or cheat
the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter, a standard crossword trick

explanation.surface: A cheating partner feels remorse and tries to cover up for a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' reads as one word, a lover, but splits into 'sweet' and 'heart', the middle of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Shame is the painful feeling of guilt about wrongdoing, closely allied to remorse, which is deep regret for it.

clue.text: Top gallery showing film

parts.note: ace means top, first-rate
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A leading art gallery is screening a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie in the cinema sense, but it means a thin transparent sheet. The Tate is a group of major British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a cellulose plastic made into thin transparent sheets, used for photographic film and overhead transparencies.

clue.text: Superior sailor meets Virgin Queen

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
Good Queen Bess, Elizabeth I, was known as the Virgin Queen

explanation.surface: A high-ranking seaman is granted an audience with Elizabeth I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' looks like an adjective describing the sailor, but it is a noun: the head of a religious house, as in Mother Superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mother Superior heads a convent of nuns, and the woman in charge of an abbey holds exactly that position.

clue.text: Undergarment that is about below neck

indicators.note: in a down clue, whatever is below something is written after it in the grid

parts.note: brass and neck are both slang for cheek or nerve
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An item of underwear that sits a little below the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' seems anatomical, beside the undergarment, but means nerve or effrontery. Having the brass neck to do something is British for having the cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is the full name of the bra, a woman's supporting undergarment for the breasts.

clue.text: Cry wolf, perhaps, in account

indicators.note: something in another thing sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: an entry is an account or record, as in a ledger or diary
to wolf food is one way to eat it, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A tale about the boy who cried wolf, told as a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the fable, but 'Cry' is a noun meaning an appeal, and 'wolf' is the verb for gobbling food.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea, and a cry in the sense of an urgent appeal for help is just that.

clue.text: Piercing Spartacus finally with spear

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter of the gladiator's name
a trident is a three-pronged spear, as used by some Roman gladiators

explanation.surface: The gladiator Spartacus is finally stabbed with a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piercing' sits beside the spear as if it were a wound, but it describes a loud, harsh sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A piercing voice or noise is shrill and grating, and a harsh, loud sound is exactly what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Shocks holding resistance in power cuts

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: outages are failures of the electricity supply
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Electrical shocks from resistance during a power failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocks' and 'resistance' suggest electricity, but the definition means scandals. Outage is the usual American word for a power cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is something that causes public indignation or scandal, much as a shock is a startling, upsetting event.

clue.text: Bird carried away by old rook

parts.note: rapt means enraptured, carried away with delight
O is the abbreviation for old
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A bird snatched away by an old rook, itself a kind of crow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' wants to be the crow beside 'Bird', but it is the chess piece, abbreviated as in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A raptor is a bird of prey, such as a hawk, eagle or falcon, so it is a specific kind of bird.

clue.text: Notice following raised charges

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it in the answer

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters makes them read upwards, which turns them backwards

parts.note: to notice something is to see it

explanation.surface: A notice informing customers that prices have gone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' does double duty in the sense that it is both the abbreviation F and its position; 'raised charges' reads as higher prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Fees are sums of money payable for a service, which is what charges means as a plural noun.

clue.text: In budget a remuneration's backed number

indicators.note: something backed has gone backwards, so the letters are read from right to left
what is in the words is contained within them, so the letters sit inside the running text

parts.note: the letters run across the words from the end of the first to the middle of the last

explanation.surface: A sum set aside in a budget for pay is reported back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a noun, a figure in the budget, but it is the verb meaning to count.
explanation.definitionFit: To number things is to count them or list them one by one, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Went up against son in race

indicators.note: two things up against each other sit side by side, so the pieces are joined end to end

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to go, euphemistically, is to relieve oneself

explanation.surface: A parent ran against their son in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is the coy euphemism for using the toilet, and 'race' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to move very fast, and the verb for going quickly carries the same meaning.

clue.text: Queen roughly rejected port

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters go the other way

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
ca. is circa, meaning roughly

explanation.surface: Her Majesty brusquely turned down a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the drink; it is a harbour town. Acre is an ancient port city in northern Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is a historic harbour city on the Mediterranean coast of Israel, famous from the Crusades, so it is an example.

clue.text: It's nice and natural wasting time

indicators.note: wasting something means losing it, so a letter is thrown away

parts.note: congenital means inborn, natural from birth
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A relaxed remark that it is pleasant to be natural and idle.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T out of CONGENITAL. 'Natural' here means inborn, not unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenial company or surroundings are pleasant and agreeable, which is what nice means in everyday speech.

clue.text: Singular number clothing small honey?

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it up, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
wee is Scottish for small
ten is a number

explanation.surface: One particular figure dressing a little darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honey' looks like a noun or endearment; the question mark flags it as a verb, to honey something being to make it sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: To honey a drink or dish is to add sweetness to it, a rare verb sense, and the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Poles carrying strain making camp

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: bars are rods or poles
to rack is to strain, as in racking one's brains

explanation.surface: Workers hauling heavy loads on poles while setting up a camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests Polish people or tent poles; it is rods, and 'camp' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are buildings housing soldiers, and a military camp is a similar place where troops are quartered.

clue.text: Book about passion's lacking interest

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a tome is a large book
ire is anger, a passion; with the 's it reads 'ire is'

explanation.surface: A review of a book about passion that is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'passion's' is a contraction of 'is', adding the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is boring or tedious, so it fails to hold anyone's attention or curiosity.

clue.text: Joined in lair lizard rolled over

indicators.note: rolling over turns something end to end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair
the Gila monster is a venomous lizard

explanation.surface: A lizard joined others in its lair and rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gila monster is a lizard of the American south-west, named after the Gila river.
explanation.definitionFit: Aligned means allied or associated with a group, as non-aligned nations are not joined to any bloc.

clue.text: Puppet dancing on long lines, initially?

definitions.text: Puppet dancing on long lines, initially?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A marionette jigs about on long strings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of the answer: a puppet figure dangling on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a figure of a person moved by strings, a jointed toy figure like a child's plaything.

clue.text: Munch cold chop

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to hew is to chop with an axe

explanation.surface: Eating a cold pork chop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop' looks like a cut of meat to munch, but it is the verb meaning to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To munch is to eat with steady, noisy jaw movements, which is to grind food with the teeth.

clue.text: Admit prisoner with iron shackles, gutted

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: a gutted thing has had its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters once the middle is taken out

explanation.surface: Let in a prisoner wearing iron shackles who is utterly dejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British slang for devastated, which suits the prisoner, but it empties the shackles. 'Admit' also misleads as 'let in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit a fault or crime is to own up to it, which is exactly the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Touch of caution's gripping socialist's leader

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it tight inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: care is caution; with the 's it reads 'care is'

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so just the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hint of wariness has taken hold of a left-wing party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch' reads as a small amount, as in a touch of caution, but it is the gentle stroke that is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle, affectionate stroke, so it is a particular loving kind of touch.

clue.text: Raise possibly from gambler

definitions.meaning: first meaning: improve, of which raising standards is one example

explanation.surface: A gambler might raise the stakes at the poker table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' looks like the poker move, but here it means to improve, one example of the verb, hence 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means improve, which raising standards does; as a noun it is someone who places wagers.

clue.text: Empty role with first female magistrate

indicators.note: an empty word has nothing in its middle, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters with the inside removed
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A token post held by the first woman magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First female' looks like a pioneering woman in office, but it is Eve. A reeve was a medieval English local official.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a chief officer of a town or district in Anglo-Saxon England, with judicial powers, so a historical magistrate.

clue.text: View of loch including small head

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for loch, as on maps
and means plus or including
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: A scenic view over a Scottish lake with a little promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Including' looks like a container signal, but it simply gives AND. 'Head' is a headland, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is an extensive stretch of scenery seen from one place, or a painting of it, hence a view.

clue.text: Rocked for the audience in leather?

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: rocked means moved to and fro

explanation.surface: A rock band played to the crowd wearing leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocked' and 'audience' suggest a gig; it means moved from side to side. The question mark marks the answer as one kind of leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped, velvety surface, so it is one example of the material, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Feature about work revealing composer

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
op. is opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature article about a piece of music reveals its composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' reads as an article; it is a part of the face. OP for opus is apt for a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was the Polish Romantic composer famed for piano works, so he is one example of a composer.

clue.text: Housing people imprisoned by conviction

indicators.note: something imprisoned is locked inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a tenet is a belief or conviction
men are people

explanation.surface: Accommodation for those jailed after a criminal conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conviction' suggests a court sentence to go with imprisonment, but it means a firmly held belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, especially rented and crowded ones, so a form of residential accommodation.

clue.text: Recites letters in order for incantations

definitions.meaning: first meaning: names the letters of a word one by one
second meaning: magic formulas spoken aloud

explanation.surface: A wizard chants the alphabet in sequence to work magic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one act of a magician, but it splits into a verb and a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means naming a word's letters in sequence; as a noun it means magic words or charms.

clue.text: Trespasses sorted involving judge

indicators.note: something involving another wraps it up within itself, so the letters lie inside the text

parts.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Trespassing offences are dealt with by a court judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted' looks like an anagram signal, but nothing is shuffled: the letters lie in plain sight across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor is someone who evaluates or estimates value, or advises a judge in court, so to judge is the role.
